Convert an ALS fit to MCMC starting values

Source: R/als_start_vals.R
als_start_vals.Rd

Builds a start_vals list for ame or lame from the estimates of an ALS fit. This is useful when the ALS fit has already found a good latent-space solution and the MCMC chain should start near that solution rather than from diffuse random values.

Usage

als_start_vals(fit, jitter = 0, seed = NULL)

Arguments

fit

a fitted ame_als, lame_als, or dynamic ALS object returned by lame with method = "als".

jitter

non-negative standard deviation for independent Gaussian perturbations added to numeric starting values. Use a small positive value for multiple MCMC chains.

seed

optional integer seed used for the jitter.

Value

A list that can be passed to start_vals. For a dynamic ALS fit it also carries rho_uv, sigma_uv, rho_ab, and sigma_ab, so the MCMC run starts its AR(1) hyperparameters from the ALS solution. The dyadic rho start is the single pooled correlation in fit$VC["rho"], matching ALS simulation. Period-specific rho_path / residual_rho_path values are residual diagnostics, including in legacy objects labelled dynamic_rho = TRUE, and are not used as covariance-path starting values. A MCMC model requesting dynamic_rho = TRUE expands this scalar initial value; explicit MCMC path starts remain available through its start_vals argument. For a dynamic empirical-Bayes fit these are estimates under the lame() hyperpriors. For a binary fit the intercept is shifted so that the implied tie rate, mean(pnorm(EZ)), equals the observed one, with everything else held at the ALS values; the shift is stored in attr(, "level_shift"). The ALS intercept sits within a few hundredths of the level the sampler has to reach.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 12
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * n), n, n); diag(Y) <- NA
fit_als <- ame_als(Y, R = 1, family = "normal", verbose = FALSE)
sv <- als_start_vals(fit_als)
# chains = 1 keeps the example short; the default runs two chains and compares them
fit_mcmc <- ame(Y, R = 1, start_vals = sv,
                nscan = 20, burn = 5, odens = 1, verbose = FALSE, chains = 1)
